From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Rappel and ráppel

English

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from French rappeler (“to pull through (a rope)”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɹæˈpɛl/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛl

Noun

[edit]

rappel (plural rappels)

  1. Descending by means of a rope, abseiling.

Verb

[edit]

rappel (third-person singular simple present rappels, present participle rappelling, simple past and past participle rappelled)

  1. To abseil.
  2. (obsolete) To call back a hawk.
Derived terms
[edit]
  • rappeller
Translations
[edit]
to abseil
  • Bulgarian: рапел m (rapel)
  • Czech: slaňovat impf, slanit pf
  • Dutch: abseilen (nl)
  • French: descendre en rappel
  • Polish: opuszczać się przy pomocy liny impf, opuścić się przy pomocy liny pf
  • Russian: спуска́ться на верёвке (spuskátʹsja na verjóvke)
  • Spanish: rápel (es)
  • Swedish: fira ner sig (sv), fira sig ner (sv)
  • Ukrainian: спускатися по мотузці (spuskatysja po motuzci)

Further reading

[edit]
  • rappel on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

Etymology 2

[edit]

Borrowed from French rappel. Compare repeal.

Noun

[edit]

rappel (plural rappels)

  1. (military) A drumbeat pattern for calling soldiers to gather.
    • 1839, Fraser's Magazine for Town and Country, volume 19, page 711:
      […] he has to retramp the same streets, rebeat the same rappel […]

Anagrams

[edit]
  • lapper

Basque

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish rappel, from French rappeler.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /rapel/ [ra.pel]
  • Rhymes: -apel, -el

Noun

[edit]

rappel inan

  1. (climbing) rappel

French

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ʁa.pɛl/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Hérault)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

rappel m (plural rappels)

  1. reminder
  2. encore (at the end of a performance); curtain call
  3. (on a speed limit sign) continuance of an existing speed limit
  4. (transitive) (A faulty product) subject to a recall. [from 20th c.]
    Veuillez nous le notifier immédiatement si vous savez ou suspectez qu'un produit puisse ou doive faire l'objet d'un rappel.
    Please notify us immediately if you suspect there is a possibility of products needing to become the subject of a recall.
  5. abseil

Derived terms

[edit]
  • piqûre de rappel
  • pour rappel

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Catalan: ràpel
  • → Dutch: rappel
    • → Indonesian: rapel
  • → English: rappel
  • → Portuguese: rapel
  • → Romanian: rapel
  • → Spanish: rapel

Further reading

[edit]
  • “rappel”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Anagrams

[edit]
  • palper
